transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, I'm here because... I just can't stop thinking about how I look. I work as a host at a restaurant, and I'm constantly fixated on my hairline and the way my face looks under the lights there. I feel like I look really old and just... strange. It takes up a lot of my thoughts. My coworkers tell me they don't see what I'm talking about, but I just can't get past it.

When your coworkers tell you they don't notice anything unusual about your appearance, do you think it's possible they're right and you might be misjudging how you look, or do you feel certain that your perception is accurate no matter what they say?

I'm... I honestly don't know. I mean, when they say that, I try to believe them, and a part of me wonders if maybe I am just misjudging it. But then I look in the mirror or catch my reflection at work, and the flaws just seem so obvious to me. So I'm really not sure. I don't know if they're just being polite to make me feel better, or if I'm actually seeing it wrong.

Aside from these concerns about your appearance, have you noticed anything else unusual lately — like hearing or seeing things others don't, or having thoughts or beliefs that seem to come out of nowhere and that others find strange?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear or see things that aren't there, and... I don't think I have any other strange beliefs. It's really just the stuff with my face and my hair. That's what takes up all my mental energy. But as far as everything else you just mentioned, no, I haven't experienced any of that.
